text: REST APIs allow applications to communicate with each other over the internet. When designing them, you should create clear and logical endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found, so clients understand what happened. Good documentation helps other developers use your API without confusion. You should also plan for versioning, for example by adding /v1/ to the URL, so future changes do not break existing users. Following these practices makes your API easier to maintain and more reliable for everyone.
